english.title: Permit the destruction / suppression of a document stored in compliance with Community Rules - Transport Act 1968
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) permitted to be destroyed or suppressed data, namely **(..SPECIFY THE DATA..), stored in compliance with the requirements of the applicable Community rules, on

(A)_[recording equipment]_
(B)_[a driver card]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 99ZE(3)(e) and (5) of the Transport Act 1968.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Subsection 99ZE(10) of the Transport Act 1968 provides that for the purposes of this offence, a person shall be taken to permit an act or omission if he is, or ought reasonably to be, aware of the act or omission, or of it being a likelihood, and takes no steps to prevent it.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
